neighbours.label: the comma closing an introductory phrase or clause before the main clause
fire: Not wanting to be late for the interview because of the traffic, I left the house an hour early.
With a strong cast and a clever script, the play sold out every night.
Given the rising cost of fuel and the long winter ahead, the town bought extra wood.
After weeks of rain and flooding along the coast, the farmers finally planted.
Because of the heavy snow that fell overnight, the school stayed closed.
Despite the noise from the construction next door, she finished her novel.
With a big kitchen and a garden full of herbs, this cottage is perfect for cooks.
Worried about the storm and the rising river, the family moved upstairs.
quiet: I left the house an hour early because I did not want to be late for the interview.
The play sold out every night thanks to a strong cast and a clever script.
The town bought extra wood because fuel was costly and the winter was long.
The farmers finally planted after weeks of rain and flooding along the coast.
The school stayed closed because of the heavy snow that fell overnight.
She finished her novel despite the noise from the construction next door.
This cottage is perfect for cooks who want a big kitchen and a garden full of herbs.
The family moved upstairs because they worried about the storm and the river.
